subject: Private VPC: reference matrix, control/data-plane validation & fallback runbook
content:
From: CloudOps Solutions <eng-ops@cloudops.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: itprocure@acme-health.com
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC design kickoff and sample topology

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the quick intro call last week. Acme's network team asked us to share a starter topology and a short checklist so they can validate the control-/data-plane boundaries before the vendor security review.

What's most useful for them right now: a single-page reference matrix mapping: control-plane endpoints (FQDNs/ports), data-plane egress rules, allowed CIDR ranges, NAT/egress patterns for on-prem workers, and an explicit fallback path if private peering fails (they prefer documented behaviour for burst/bypass).

We can host a short review session this week if you want — Thurs morning PT worked well for their infra folks.

Attached: sample-topology-v1.png (simple sketch).

Best,
Sam
CloudOps Solutions

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: CloudOps Solutions <eng-ops@cloudops.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private VPC design kickoff and sample topology

Sam — thanks for the note and helpful starter.

High level response: we can provide the exact control-plane hostnames and ports (control plane API, auth, telemetry ingestion) and a recommended set of SNAT/DNS configurations for on-prem inference nodes. Important callouts:

- We keep control-plane traffic strictly outbound from customer VPC to our control endpoint (no inbound control-plane listeners).
- Data-plane (inference) egress depends on deployment mode: for our VPC-attached Private deployment we support (1) routed peering (VPC peering or transit) or (2) encrypted relay via outbound proxy (TLS + mTLS to Redwood relay).
- Fallback behaviour: if peering path fails, ops can toggle an ingress-relay fallback that routes inference requests through our regional public relays with customer-level auth and IP allowlisting. This adds latency but preserves availability.

I'm attaching a short reference matrix and a control/data-plane diagram (v2). Kim will follow up with port-level details and a canary rollout runbook for the fallback.

Can you confirm Thurs 09:00 PT (2028-04-03 09:00 PDT) for a 30-min technical review?

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: vpc-reference-matrix.xlsx, control-dataplane-diagram-v2.png

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, CloudOps Solutions <eng-ops@cloudops.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private VPC design kickoff and sample topology

Adding a couple of quick technical clarifications before the review:

- Control-plane endpoints: we publish stable DNS names per-region with failover VIPs. Customers should allow outbound TLS (443) to the listed hostnames; we use ALPN to negotiate protocol. No static IPs guaranteed except for Dedicated contracts.
- Port list includes: 443 (control API), 8443 (telemetry ingestion), 22/2200 only for pre-authorised maintenance (rare).
- Data-plane egress: inference nodes will need outbound TCP to our model pull endpoints and to the relay endpoints. Blocks that restrict DNS or deep packet inspection can break model pull; recommend allowing domain-level egress or proxy bypass for those hostnames.

I'll run the canary sequencing in the runbook with Rishi.

-Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: CloudOps Solutions <eng-ops@cloudops.com>, mina_haddad@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private VPC design kickoff and sample topology (attachments: reference matrix + runbook)

Hi all — attaching the deliverables Sam requested. Quick notes inline in the matrix and runbook:

- vpc-reference-matrix.xlsx: sheet tabs = control-plane, data-plane-egress, dns-and-snat, fallback-behaviour. Each control-plane entry includes expected TLS SNI, canonical DNS, port, and a short mitigation if filtered.
- control-dataplane-diagram-v2.png: annotated with proxy vs peering paths.
- fallback-rollout-runbook.pdf: 6 steps. The core idea: validate failure, toggle fallback routing via customer console or API, run health-check probe set (we include curlable endpoints), then gradually increase load to normal over 3 canary stages.

Two operational caveats:
1) For customers using strict egress allowlists, provide the relay cert fingerprint ahead of time for pinning.
2) If the customer’s IPS/IDS performs TLS interception, we recommend a short maintenance window to add exceptions (we provide fingerprints and a simple verification script).

If Thurs 09:00 PT works, I can walk through the matrix and runbook in 20 minutes and leave 10 minutes for network team Q&A.

-Kim
Network Security Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments (stubs): control-dataplane-diagram-v2.png (image/png), vpc-reference-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), fallback-rollout-runbook.pdf (application/pdf)
